mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and increases S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If 20-day S&P 500 returns are not higher than baseline during low FEDFUNDS periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days when UNRATE exceeds 5%.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 returns are positive in >60% of cases when UNRATE triggers.

mechanism_narrative: When federal funds rate is high and unemployment is low, tighter monetary policy may slow growth, decreasing S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing GDP growth indicates weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days in late-cycle expansions.
failure_condition: If 60-day returns are positive when GDPC1 slows (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment suggests economic strength, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If 20-day returns are not higher during employment growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production suggests strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days when INDPRO exceeds 105.
failure_condition: If returns are negative in >60% of triggered cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts and low federal funds rate indicate strong demand and cheap credit, boosting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating retail sales signal strong consumer demand, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 60 days in early-cycle recoveries.
failure_condition: If 60-day returns are not higher during RSAFS growth (t-test p > 0.05).
